capitals.name: Vic (Vicus, Ausona)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Vic'; coordinates 41°55'49"N 2°15'17"E from the town page, which gives the early name 'Auso ... Vicus Ausonae'. The page says the viscounts held the region 'on behalf of the counts, who were usually resident in Barcelona'.

correction.text: Vic, Cardona and Casserès and the pagus of Berga, 798-825, before the rebellion of 826 took the county (and before Berga was detached in 990)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the infobox gives 'Established: 798' and the text says that in 798 Louis of Aquitaine ordered Borrell to repair the castles of Vic, Cardona and Casserès, but Cliopatria's first shape is 990. The 990 outline is used as the core, with the pagus of Berga added (its extent is not on the page, so the Berguedà comarca stands in for it). Fix pass 2026-10-25 (reviewer's blocking finding): the shape now ends in 825, because the page says 'After the rebellion of 826, during which Guillemó and Aissó succeeded in taking it with help from the Emirate of Córdoba' and 'Osona remained depopulated and outside of Frankish control until 879'; nothing is drawn for 826-878 and the county is drawn again from 879 (keyframe county-of-osona_879). The reviewer asked for the keyframe to end 'at 826'; 825 is the last year held, so that 826, the year of the loss event, is the first year not drawn (the 990 loss of Berga likewise has its keyframe end in 989). The page also says Osona 'was considered to be part of the County of Barcelona' throughout the tenth century, so its separate colour from 879 to 989 is the dossier's convention; Cliopatria's Barcelona shapes of 898, 950 and 989 do not overlap it (checked with the gazetteer). The County of Manresa page adds that 'The castle at Manresa dates from the last quarter of the ninth century' and that Wilfred attached the Moianés and Bages to Osona, so the Manresa (Bages) end of the 990 outline is probably later than 798; the page names Vic, Cardona and Casserès only for 798.

correction.text: the county as repopulated from 879: Vic, Cardona and Casserès with the pagus of Berga, before Berga was detached in 990

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 879, Wilfred the Hairy began the repopulation of the county with free minores', ending the years when Osona 'remained depopulated and outside of Frankish control' (826-878, nothing drawn). The outline is the same as keyframe county-of-osona_798 (Cliopatria's 990 shape plus the pagus of Berga): the page gives no boundary for 879 and Cliopatria has no Osona shape before 990. Added in the fix pass of 2026-10-25.

2,329 km2, 990-999: the country round Vic, Manresa and Cardona (bbox 41.7-42.3 N, 1.4-2.9 E). The infobox gives no area, so there is no area check. The page: 'In 990, the small pagus of Berga was detached from it and granted to Cerdanya', which is the year the Cliopatria shape starts.
2,257 km2, 1000-1002: the outline moves slightly east and north (to 2.94 E, 42.37 N); no page dates a boundary change in 1000. Kept as drawn.

1,454 km2, 1003-1027: the western third (west of 2.08 E, the Manresa and Cardona side) is gone, so the shape is about Osona proper, with Vic inside it (checked with the gazetteer). No page dates this loss. The page says only that Osona was later 'augmented by the addition of the County of Manresa, which was subsumed within Osona'. Kept; the ledger bridges the change at confidence 1.

New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Osona shape between 1028 and 1039, yet the page has the county continuing (counts of Barcelona 943-1035; 'In 1035, Osona was detached from Barcelona for another brief period when Berenguer Ramon I left it to his widow'). The 1003 outline is held across the gap.

2,217 km2, 1040-1055: the western part is back (to 1.21 E), which matches the page's 'augmented by the addition of the County of Manresa, which was subsumed within Osona'. The page does not date the addition and, by its order of sentences, puts it after the 1035-1054 interval of Guisla and William; Cliopatria has it in 1040-1055 only. Unsettled; kept as drawn.

1,454 km2, 1056-1098, the 1003 outline again: Manresa is out of the shape. If the page's sentence about Manresa follows the 1054 reunion with Barcelona, the larger outline of 1040 should stand here instead; the page does not say, so Cliopatria's shape is kept and the question is left to the gap-fillers.

correction.text: unchanged geometry, valid 1099-1111: the county ends in 1111

keyframe_review.note: 1,454 km2, 1099-1110. The page makes Bernard III of Besalú the 'last de facto count' (1107-1111) and says Osona 'Became a permanent territory of the Principality of Catalonia: 1111', so the life runs one year past Cliopatria's last shape.

ledger.note: 798: Louis of Aquitaine sets Borrell to rebuild Vic, Cardona and Casserès, and the county begins. Infobox 'Established: 798'; 'Its reconquest by Christian powers began in 798; in that year Louis of Aquitaine ordered' the castles repaired, and 'Vic was in Frankish hands by 799.' The infobox says 'Preceded by Al-Andalus'. The page gives the three castles, not a boundary; the region is Cliopatria's 990 shape. Reviewer 2026-10-25: counterpart 'nobody' (was emirate-of-cordoba), because the page has Louis order Borrell 'to enter the abandoned region'.
801: Borrell is made Count of Osona. 'After the successful siege of Barcelona in 801, Borrell, already Count of Cerdanya and Urgell, received Osona as a countship' from the king.

region.text: the county as held since 798, taken in the rebellion of 826

ledger.note: 826: Guillemó and Aissó take Osona in their rebellion. 'After the rebellion of 826, during which Guillemó and Aissó succeeded in taking it with help from the Emirate of Córdoba'; the page's list gives Aissó and Guillemó as counts 826-827, and the county then 'remained depopulated and outside of Frankish control until 879', so nothing is drawn 826-878. The Aissó page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aisso): 'Ayxun or Aissó was a nobleman who led a revolt in Barcelona, Ausona, and Girona in 826 to 827.' The counterpart is the rebels, who left no state and no dossier. Region: Cliopatria's 990 shape plus the pagus of Berga, as in keyframe county-of-osona_798. Added in the fix pass of 2026-10-25 (reviewer's blocking finding); the old 827 rename moved to 879.

879: Wilfred the Hairy begins the repopulation of Osona. 'In 879, Wilfred the Hairy began the repopulation of the county with free minores'; until then 'Osona remained depopulated and outside of Frankish control'. The land comes back from no state (counterpart nobody). Region: the same as the 826 loss. Added in the fix pass of 2026-10-25.

879: Osona is held by the counts of Barcelona (the page's list: counts of Barcelona 827-939, Ermengol 939-943, counts of Barcelona 943-1035). 'Throughout the tenth century, Osona remained tied to Barcelona' and 'It was considered to be part of the County of Barcelona throughout that period.' Moved from 827 in the fix pass of 2026-10-25: the title passed to Barcelona in 827, but the land was outside Frankish control until 879. Same state, same colour (rule 2); the years are the list's.

990: the pagus of Berga leaves Osona. 'In 990, the small pagus of Berga was detached from it and granted to Cerdanya.' Cliopatria's County of Berga is the Cerdanya-side county; the pagus's extent is not given, so the Berguedà comarca stands in for it.

region.text: the western part of the 1002 shape (Manresa and Cardona side), absent from the 1003 shape

ledger.note: 1003: the western third of the shape is gone in Cliopatria. The page is silent on any 1003 event (Almanzor does not appear on it); the year is Cliopatria's and the 'County of Manresa' is only the page's name for the land it later says was 'subsumed within Osona'. Fix pass 2026-10-25: the English County of Manresa page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_of_Manresa) gives no year for any union with Osona; it says 'The County of Ausona was thus born and to it Wilfred attached the Moianés and Bages', calls Manresa 'the western extremity of the County of Osona, divided into the Moianès and Bages', and says 'it never had a viscount'. So the page treats the Manresa country as part of Osona from 879 (the repopulation), not as a separate county added in the eleventh century, and does not explain Cliopatria's coming and going of the western part; the event stays a confidence-1 bridge of Cliopatria's outline, and 'County of Manresa' is only the page's name for that land (no separate dossier is needed).

1035: Guisla de Lluçà and her son William rule Osona. 'In 1035, Osona was detached from Barcelona for another brief period when Berenguer Ramon I left it to his widow,' Guisla (the list: Guisla de Lluça and William 1035-1054).

region.text: the western part, 'the County of Manresa, which was subsumed within Osona'

ledger.note: 1040: Osona is 'augmented by the addition of the County of Manresa, which was subsumed within Osona'. The page gives no year; 1040 is Cliopatria's. The page's order of sentences may put it after 1054 (see the 1056 verdict). Fix pass 2026-10-25: the English County of Manresa page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_of_Manresa) gives no year for any union with Osona; it says 'The County of Ausona was thus born and to it Wilfred attached the Moianés and Bages', calls Manresa 'the western extremity of the County of Osona, divided into the Moianès and Bages', and says 'it never had a viscount'. So the page treats the Manresa country as part of Osona from 879 (the repopulation), not as a separate county added in the eleventh century, and does not explain Cliopatria's coming and going of the western part; the event stays a confidence-1 bridge of Cliopatria's outline, and 'County of Manresa' is only the page's name for that land (no separate dossier is needed).
1054: Osona returns to the counts of Barcelona (the page's list: counts of Barcelona 1054-1107); the year is the list's.

region.text: the western part, absent from the 1056 shape

ledger.note: 1056: Cliopatria's shape drops back to the 1003 outline. The page does not say that Manresa left Osona (it says the opposite order); bridging only. Fix pass 2026-10-25: the English County of Manresa page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_of_Manresa) gives no year for any union with Osona; it says 'The County of Ausona was thus born and to it Wilfred attached the Moianés and Bages', calls Manresa 'the western extremity of the County of Osona, divided into the Moianès and Bages', and says 'it never had a viscount'. So the page treats the Manresa country as part of Osona from 879 (the repopulation), not as a separate county added in the eleventh century, and does not explain Cliopatria's coming and going of the western part; the event stays a confidence-1 bridge of Cliopatria's outline, and 'County of Manresa' is only the page's name for that land (no separate dossier is needed).

1107: Osona goes to the Count of Besalú. 'Ramon Berenguer III ceded the county to his son-in-law Bernard III of Besalú, as dowry of his daughter Jimena in 1107.' A change of holder, not of state (rule 2); Besalú is not otherwise merged.

1111: Osona becomes a permanent part of Catalonia. 'When both Jimena and Bernard died without heirs, Osona returned to Barcelona.' Infobox 'Became a permanent territory of the Principality of Catalonia: 1111'; Bernard III is 'last de facto count', 1107-1111.

1111: the County of Osona ends; 'The "county" and "count" of Osona disappeared as distinct terms after 1107-1111.' The title was revived for the Cabrera family in 1356 without any rule over the region.

wars.name: Revolt of Aissó and Guillemó

zones.text: the county taken by the rebels in 826

wars.outcome: 'After the rebellion of 826, during which Guillemó and Aissó succeeded in taking it with help from the Emirate of Córdoba'; Osona then 'remained depopulated and outside of Frankish control until 879'.
wars.note: The Aissó page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aisso) dates the revolt 826 to 827 in Barcelona, Ausona and Girona, and has the emirate's general Ubayd Allah arrive at Zaragoza in May 827 and attack Girona on 10 October 827. It does not say who put the revolt down; the war ends in 827, the last year the Osona page's list gives Aissó and Guillemó as counts. No contest events are entered, because the land was lost outright in 826 (loss event). Added in the fix pass of 2026-10-25.

wars.name: Almanzor's sack of Barcelona (985)
wars.outcome: 'In 985 Barcelona, then ruled by Borrell II, was attacked and burned by Muslims, led by Almanzor'; the count took refuge in the Montserrat mountains.
wars.note: Listed because Osona was 'part of the County of Barcelona' in the tenth century. The Osona page does not mention Almanzor, and no page opened places the raid in Osona, so no zone.

notes: County of Osona 798-1111 (Cliopatria 990-1110 with a gap 1028-1039). Page budget 5; five pages opened (one a disambiguation page, one failed). UNSETTLED: (1) Start: the infobox says 798 but Cliopatria begins 990, and the page says Osona 'was considered to be part of the County of Barcelona' throughout the tenth century; the dossier follows the infobox and draws Osona as its own colour from 798 (new keyframe 798-989). If the colour agent or the Barcelona dossier treats the 10th-century Osona as Barcelona's land, drop the 798 and 879 keyframes and the 879 rename; Cliopatria's pre-990 Barcelona shapes do not overlap it. (2) The Manresa question: Cliopatria's western part of the shape comes and goes (990-1002, 1040-1055); the page says only that Osona 'was augmented by the addition of the County of Manresa', undated and after the 1035-1054 interval; the three ledger events about it (1003, 1040, 1056) are confidence 1 and may be wrong in direction. (3) The Guisla de Lluçà page failed to load; the 1035-1054 interval rests on the County of Osona page alone. (4) The page's list says Ximena 1107-1149, which conflicts with the text that Osona returned to Barcelona when Jimena and Bernard died; 1111 (infobox) is kept. (5) The pagus of Berga's extent is not on the page; Berguedà stands in. (6) Counterparts needing dossiers: County of Manresa (a name only; no Cliopatria row). Gazetteer names used that it lacks: Berguedà (region). Cliopatria's Berga and Cerdanya rows are another batch's. FIX PASS 2026-10-25 (author, after the reviewer's FAIL): (a) The reviewer's blocking finding was right: the page has Osona taken in the rebellion of 826 and 'depopulated and outside of Frankish control until 879'. Added a loss in 826 (counterpart the rebels, confidence 3), a gain in 879 (counterpart nobody, confidence 3), the war 'Revolt of Aissó and Guillemó' 826-827, a second keyframe county-of-osona_879 (879-989) and moved the 'counts of Barcelona' rename from 827 to 879; keyframe county-of-osona_798 now ends in 825 (the reviewer said 826; 825 keeps the keyframe and the 826 loss event in step). Nothing is drawn for 826-878. The Aissó page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aisso) was opened for the war's dates; it dates the revolt 826 to 827 but is silent on how Osona was lost, so the 826 loss rests on the County of Osona page. (b) Thin item, Manresa (1003, 1040, 1056 at confidence 1): the Catalan page https://ca.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comtat_de_Manresa could not be read (url_not_found on two tries), so the Guisla de Lluçà interval stays as it was. The English County of Manresa page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_of_Manresa) was opened instead: it dates no union, and says Wilfred attached the Moianés and Bages to Ausona (879) and that Manresa was Osona's western extremity, so the page does not support a separate County of Manresa. The three Manresa events (1003, 1040, 1056) stay at confidence 1 with this added to their notes; 'County of Manresa' needs no dossier. (c) The reviewer's counterpart change on the 798 found event (nobody) is kept.
